blocks.text: Mesh Routing moves events between devices and services. This page covers what an event looks like and what happens after you send one.
Every event has two parts: an envelope, which Mesh Routing reads, and a body, which it carries without reading.
id: a unique id set by the sender. Use it to spot repeats.
sender: the device or service sending the event.
destination: where the event should be delivered.
schema_version: the version of the body's format, set by the sender.
sent_at: when the sender sent the event.
The body is yours. Mesh Routing doesn't inspect or change it, and doesn't need to know its format.
The receiver acknowledges each event by its id. Until an event is acknowledged, Mesh Routing keeps it.
If an event isn't acknowledged, Mesh Routing retries with backoff: a short wait at first, then longer ones, up to a limit you set. Receivers should treat a repeated id as already handled.
